sn12.22:1.1: Near Sāvatthī … the Exalted One said:
sn12.22:1.2: “Monks, the Tathāgata, endowed with the ten powers and the four confidences … turns the Divine Wheel:
sn12.22:1.3: Such is material shape: and so on.
sn12.22:1.8: So 'this' being, 'that' becomes; from the arising of this, that arises;
sn12.22:1.9: 'this' not being, that becomes not; from the ceasing of this, that ceases. That is to say:
sn12.22:1.11: Conditioned by activities, consciousness … name-and-shape, sense, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, old age-and-death, and grief, lamenting, suffering, sorrow, despair come to pass.
sn12.22:1.12: Such is the uprising of this entire mass of ill.
sn12.22:1.13: But from the utter fading away and ceasing of ignorance, activities cease,
sn12.22:1.14: and thus ceases each of the rest. …
sn12.22:1.15: Such is the ceasing of this entire mass of ill.
sn12.22:2.1: Thus, Monks, the Dhamma being well declared by me, made manifest, disclosed, brought to light, stripped of its swathing,
sn12.22:2.2: it is enough for the clansman who has left the world through faith to stir up energy and vow:
sn12.22:2.3: 'Let skin and sinews and bones wilt in my body, let flesh and blood dry up, yet shall there be upkeep of energy till I have won that which by man's strength, by man's energy, by man's progress may be won!'
sn12.22:3.1: Sadly, Monks, lives the man of sloth, involved in bad, wicked things. Great is the salvation which he fails to win.
sn12.22:3.2: But he of stirred up energy lives happily, aloof from bad, wicked things. Great is the salvation that he makes perfect.
sn12.22:3.3: Not by that which is low, Monks, may the highest be won;
sn12.22:3.4: by that which is highest may the highest be won.
sn12.22:3.5: Worthy of praise, Monks, is this divine life. The Teacher has come to you face to face.
sn12.22:3.6: Wherefore stir up energy that you may win what is not won, that you may attain what is not attained, that you may realize what is unrealized, thinking:
sn12.22:3.7: 'Thus will this our leaving the world not be barren, but a fruitful and a growing thing.
sn12.22:3.8: The necessaries that we enjoy: the equipment of robes, alms, lodging and medicine, though they be humble, shall be to us of great profit and advantage.'
sn12.22:3.9: For thus, Monks, must you train yourselves:
sn12.22:3.10: If a man discerns his own good, this is enough to call up earnestness;
sn12.22:3.11: if he discerns another's good, this is enough to call up earnestness;
sn12.22:3.12: if he discerns both his own and another's good, this is enough to call up earnestness.
